## Assumptions

- This workspace is an intentional eval harness — it contains no app code, APK/AAB, or build project (`README.md` confirms "empty on purpose").
- No Android device or emulator is attached (`adb` is absent; no `.apk`/`.aab` anywhere in the tree).

## Hard blocker — read this first

I **cannot produce actual test results**. There is no app artifact to install and no device/emulator to run it on, so any "pass/fail" I reported would be fabricated. What I can do — and what this environment is set up for — is deliver the exact, executable test protocol for the four conditions you named, with the pass conditions the skill requires. Run it once a real build + device exist; every item below is written so it can be executed and recorded as-is.

I checked the skill's `references/adaptive-ui.md` (§10 adaptive QA matrix), `references/ux-checklist.md` (§4 a11y, §5 store-sensitive, §7 perf), `references/mobile-testing.md`, and `agents/07-reviewer.md`. Everything below is drawn from those.

---

## Combined scenario: low-end Android + Reduce Motion + 200% text + location denied

This is one of the hardest real-world combinations because the four axes can mask each other (e.g. a crash may be "location denied," when it's actually a 200%-text overflow on a low-tier list). Test each axis alone first, then the combination.

### 0. Environment setup (verify before testing)
- **Low-tier detection**: confirm the app's capability check reads `ActivityManager.isLowRamDevice` / `memoryClass` (< 3 GB → `Tier.LOW`). Force the tier in a test injectable if needed — never branch on device model names.
- **Reduce Motion**: set on-device (Developer options → animation scales, or Accessibility → Remove animations) and confirm the app observes `LocalMotionDurationScale` / `Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE` live, not just at cold start.
- **200% text**: Settings → Display → Font size / Display size to max (font scale `2.0`).
- **Location denied**: install, then deny location at the first prompt; also test the **blocked** state (deny + "Don't ask again" → "Enable" deep-links to `ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS`).

Record device model, Android version, RAM, font scale, animation scale, and build (release, not debug) in the report header.

### 1. Low-end Android (Tier.LOW)
- [ ] Cold start to interactive < 2 s; no full-screen spinner over cached content.
- [ ] All long lists virtualised (`LazyColumn`); no 4000 px images in small views — images decoded at display size.
- [ ] No blur/glass, no shadows > 1 px, no concurrent video + map.
- [ ] Scroll stays ≥ 30 fps floor (55 fps is the mid-tier target); no jank on the primary list.
- [ ] Motion uses fades/opacity only, 150–250 ms; no parallax, pinned scrub, or blur.
- [ ] Memory flat across 20 loop repetitions; no leaked timers/listeners.

### 2. Reduce Motion ON
- [ ] All content visible — no zero-opacity leftovers, nothing hidden behind an animation that never plays.
- [ ] No action depends on a gesture animation; the whole story is conveyed statically.
- [ ] Travel becomes a ~150 ms fade; parallax, scrub, autoplay and looping stop; **progress still updates**.
- [ ] Every custom `withAnimation` / `animate*` honours the reduced-motion signal (not just the standard APIs).
- [ ] Screen reader still announces state changes.

### 3. 200% text (font scale 2.0)
- [ ] Labels wrap, buttons grow vertically, no clipping/overlap/truncation on any screen.
- [ ] No fixed-height rows containing text; charts have a text fallba

cases.prompt: We are replacing our live React Native app with native. What must stay the same on the stores?
judgement: Says to update the existing listing, not publish a new app
cases.response:
I'll load the relevant skill for this rebuild question.
**Assumptions:** both stores (App Store + Google Play), same brands and accounts, and this is a replacement of the live app rather than a second app. No repo or console access was provided, so this is the invariant checklist — not an inventory of your specific app. Store rules are current as of the skill's 2026‑11‑16 verification.

## The one rule
**Update the existing listing. Never create a new one.** A new bundle ID/package means zero reviews, a fresh 12‑tester/14‑day Play gate, no upgrade path, and subscribers who must buy again.

## Must stay identical

| Item | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| **App record** | Existing App Store Connect app; do not press "New app" | Existing Play Console app; do not create a new app |
| **Identifier** | `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` — immutable after first upload | `applicationId` / package name |
| **Signing identity** | Same Team ID, certificate and provisioning lineage; same ASC API key | Same Play App Signing key, same upload keystore + passwords in CI |
| **Version numbers go up** | Raise `MARKETING_VERSION` and `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` | Raise `versionName` and `versionCode` |
| **Products / entitlements** | Same product IDs; read `Transaction.currentEntitlements` including `originalID`; keep "Restore purchases" | Same product IDs; `queryPurchasesAsync` on launch; same server receipt validation |
| **Deep links** | Same universal-link domains and routes, including links already in the wild | Same App Links, schemes and routes |
| **Android notification channels** | n/a | Same channel IDs, or users lose their notification preferences |
| **Sign-in methods** | Unchanged, or removed methods have an account-recovery path | Same |
| **Account deletion** | Still in-app (5.1.1(v)) | Still in-app **and** via a web link |
| **Support/legal URLs** | Must still resolve | Must still resolve |
| **Reviews and ratings** | Carry over; never ask reviewers to delete old ones | Carry over |

## Must stay functionally continuous (not necessarily byte-identical)
- **User data:** one-time reader for the old local format (AsyncStorage/SQLite/MMKKV → SwiftData/Room); versioned, idempotent cloud migration; rollback that does not lose new writes; `schema_version` flag; deletion covers the migrated copy.
- **Push:** re-register tokens on first launch of the new build and invalidate the old token server-side.
- **Extensions:** widgets, watch apps, App Clips and shortcuts still build, or are a deliberate, justified drop.
- **Declarations:** Privacy manifest / Nutrition Labels, Data safety, age/content ratings, trader status and sensitive-permission justifications must match what the *new binary* actually does — keep the answers honest, update only where SDK behaviour changed. Analytics event names need a mapping or an accepted break.
- **Minimum OS:** raise only with a migration story.

## What should change instead
Screenshots must show the new native UI before submission, "What's New" must describe the real rewrite (vague "bug fixes and performance improvements" invites 2.3 rejection), and rollout is staged — iOS 7‑day phased release, Play 5% → 20% → 50% → 100%, halted on crash-free-sessions/ANR rather than install count.

## Cutover shape
Strangler, not big-bang: maintenance release of the old app (version reporting + data-export hook) → new shell behind flags → feature-by-feature moves → billing last → staged rollout → old binary and API alive for one release cycle. Every step reversible without a store rollback.

The highest-risk silent failures are subscriber entitlements read as free, mismatched signing keys, changed bundle ID, and broken deep links. Given the repo path, I'd run `inventory-existing.mjs --src <path>` followed by the rebuild route and produce `.mobile/00-migration-plan.md` with the per-feature parity matrix.

cases.prompt: My app has accounts and email sign-in. What do I need for review?
judgement: Deletion is in-app, not only by emailing support
cases.response:
I'll treat this as a mobile app store review-readiness question (accounts + email sign-in) and use the mobile-app-factory skill to give the precise requirements.
**Assumptions** (no human to ask): you're submitting a **new app to both iOS App Store and Google Play**; sign-in is **first-party email + password** (not Google/Facebook social login); no health, location, or payment features beyond accounts. Store rules checked against `store-facts.md` (`verified_on: 2026-11-16`), which is still fresh (90-day review window) — no re-verification needed.

Because the app is gated behind login, accounts add four hard review requirements on top of the normal checklist:

## 1. Working demo credentials for the reviewer (the big one)
- **iOS:** App Store Connect → version → *App Review Information*: contact name/phone/email + **demo account username and password**. This is the #1 rejection cause under guideline 2.1 (App Completeness).
- **Play:** App content → **App access** declaration — credentials are mandatory because a feature is gated.
- The account must be live and usable for the whole review window: backend online, seeded with real data, no expired trial, and **no 2FA/email OTP the reviewer can't pass**. If sign-in is magic-link or OTP-only, either give the reviewer a password-based account, a static test code in the notes, or a documented bypass. Add a short note: "Sign in with the demo account; it has sample data." One line saves a week.

## 2. Account deletion (else rejection / suspension)
- **iOS (5.1.1(v)):** in-app deletion path wherever account creation exists.
- **Play:** in-app deletion path **and** a public web deletion link, both declared in the Data safety form.
- Common suspension cause #3 on Play is "account creation with no deletion path."

## 3. Privacy + Terms, matched to what the app actually does
- **Privacy policy URL** required on both stores; Apple also wants it linked **in the app** (5.1.1).
- **Terms of Use** must be reviewable and accepted before the user creates an account.
- Declare the data you now collect because of accounts: email address, user ID, name, and anything in user profiles — Apple **App Privacy / Nutrition Labels** (plus `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` and signatures for any auth SDK that uses required-reason APIs), Play **Data safety** form. Both must match every SDK in the build; a mismatch is a policy violation regardless of intent.

## 4. Completeness details reviewers check for logged-in apps
- No placeholder content, dead links, or empty states behind the login; screenshots show the real shipped UI.
- **iOS 4.8:** Sign in with Apple is required only if you also offer a third-party/social login (Google, Facebook, etc.). Pure email/password does not trigger it — but if your "email sign-in" is via a third-party auth provider, add Sign in with Apple.

## General gates still apply
- **Play, new personal account:** closed test with **12 testers for 14 continuous days** before production access — start the clock on the first usable build; it's the usual launch-date killer.
- Age-rating questionnaire (new 5-tier system on iOS), DSA trader status for EU, export compliance, and the dated build requirements in `store-facts.md` (Xcode 26 / iOS 26 SDK, iOS 13+ min target; Android 16 / API 36 target, Play App Signing).

**Short version:** demo login credentials in the review notes + a backend the reviewer can actually use, in-app deletion (+ web link on Play), privacy policy and Terms with accurate data declarations, and — if you add social login on iOS — Sign in with Apple. Those are the account-specific items; everything else is the standard store checklist.
